source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֤ד אַחְאָב֙ לְאִיזֶ֔בֶל אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֛ג אֶת־כָּל־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And told Ahab to Jezebel all that had done Elijah, and all how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.

en.L: And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and all how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
en.B: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, including how he had put all the prophets to the sword.
en.R: Ahab told his wife Jezebel everything Elijah had done. He told her how Elijah had killed all the prophets of Baal with the sword.

es.L: Y Acab contó a Jezabel todo lo que Elías había hecho, y todo cómo había matado a espada a todos los profetas.
es.B: Acab le contó a Jezabel todo lo que Elías había hecho, y cómo había pasado a espada a todos los profetas.
es.R: Acab le contó a su esposa Jezabel todo lo que Elías había hecho. Le contó cómo Elías había matado a espada a todos los profetas de Baal.

fr.L: Et Achab raconta à Jézabel tout ce qu’avait fait Élie, et tout ce qu’il avait fait en tuant tous les prophètes par l’épée.
fr.B: Achab raconta à Jézabel tout ce qu’Élie avait fait, et comment il avait passé tous les prophètes au fil de l’épée.
fr.R: Achab a raconté à sa femme Jézabel tout ce qu’Élie avait fait. Il lui a raconté comment Élie avait tué par l’épée tous les prophètes de Baal.

sw.L: Ahabu akamwambia Yezebeli yote aliyoyafanya Eliya, na yote jinsi alivyowaua manabii wote kwa upanga.
sw.B: Ahabu alimweleza Yezebeli yote aliyoyafanya Eliya, hata jinsi alivyowaua manabii wote kwa upanga.
sw.R: Ahabu alimweleza mkewe Yezebeli yote aliyoyafanya Eliya. Alimweleza jinsi Eliya alivyowaua kwa upanga manabii wote wa Baali.

vi.L: A-háp thuật cho Giê-sa-bên mọi điều Ê-li đã làm, và thể nào ông đã dùng gươm giết hết các nhà tiên tri.
vi.B: A-háp kể cho Giê-sa-bên mọi điều Ê-li đã làm, kể cả việc ông đã dùng gươm giết hết các nhà tiên tri.
vi.R: A-háp kể cho vợ mình là Giê-sa-bên mọi điều Ê-li đã làm. Vua kể cho bà nghe việc Ê-li đã dùng gươm giết hết các nhà tiên tri của Ba-anh.

ko.L: 그리고 아합이 엘리야가 행한 모든 것과 그가 모든 예언자를 칼로 죽인 모든 일을 이세벨에게 이야기했다.
ko.B: 아합은 엘리야가 한 모든 일과, 그가 모든 예언자를 칼로 죽인 일을 이세벨에게 이야기했다.
ko.R: 아합은 엘리야가 한 모든 일을 아내 이세벨에게 이야기했다. 엘리야가 바알의 예언자들을 모두 칼로 죽인 일도 이야기했다.

pt.L: E Acabe contou a Jezabel tudo o que Elias tinha feito, e tudo como ele tinha matado todos os profetas à espada.
pt.B: Acabe contou a Jezabel tudo o que Elias tinha feito, inclusive como ele tinha passado todos os profetas ao fio da espada.
pt.R: Acabe contou à sua mulher Jezabel tudo o que Elias tinha feito. Contou como Elias tinha matado à espada todos os profetas de Baal.

decisions.choice: all the prophets: the prophets of Baal killed at the Kishon
decisions.reason: Elijah had the prophets of Baal seized after the contest on Mount Carmel and killed them at the brook Kishon (18:40). They were Jezebel's own prophets, fed at her table (18:19), which is why the news provokes her.

decisions.choice: Jezebel: Ahab's wife, a princess of Sidon
decisions.reason: Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, and brought the worship of Baal into Israel with her (16:31). She had already been killing the LORD's prophets (18:4, 13).

decisions.choice: his wife Jezebel; the prophets of Baal
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader who Jezebel was and which prophets were killed, as 16:31 and 18:40 tell.

source.text: וַתִּשְׁלַ֤ח אִיזֶ֨בֶל֙ מַלְאָ֔ךְ אֶל־אֵלִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־יַעֲשׂ֤וּן אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִפ֔וּן כִּֽי־כָעֵ֤ת מָחָר֙ אָשִׂ֣ים אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֔ כְּנֶ֖פֶשׁ אַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Jezebel a messenger to Elijah, saying, Thus may do [the] gods and thus may they add, for about [this] time tomorrow I will make your life like [the] life of one of them.

en.L: And Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "Thus may the gods do, and thus may they add, for about [this] time tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them."
en.B: So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah to say, "May the gods deal with me ever so severely if by this time tomorrow I have not made your life like the life of one of them."
en.R: So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah with this message: "May the gods punish me terribly if by this time tomorrow I have not killed you, just as you killed those prophets!"

es.L: Y Jezabel envió un mensajero a Elías, diciendo: «Así me hagan los dioses, y así me añadan, si mañana a esta hora no he puesto tu vida como la vida de uno de ellos».
es.B: Entonces Jezabel envió un mensajero a Elías para decirle: «Que los dioses me castiguen duramente, y aun más, si mañana a esta hora no he hecho con tu vida lo que se hizo con la de uno de ellos».
es.R: Entonces Jezabel envió un mensajero a Elías con este mensaje: «¡Que los dioses me castiguen terriblemente si mañana a esta hora no te he matado, así como tú mataste a esos profetas!».

fr.L: Et Jézabel envoya un messager à Élie, en disant : « Que les dieux fassent ainsi, et qu’ils y ajoutent, car demain à pareille heure je ferai de ta vie comme la vie de l’un d’eux. »
fr.B: Jézabel envoya donc un messager dire à Élie : « Que les dieux me traitent avec sévérité, et plus encore, si demain à cette heure-ci je n’ai pas fait de ta vie ce que tu as fait de la vie de chacun d’eux. »
fr.R: Jézabel a donc envoyé un messager à Élie avec ce message : « Que les dieux me punissent sévèrement si demain à cette heure-ci je ne t’ai pas tué, comme tu as tué ces prophètes ! »

sw.L: Yezebeli akatuma mjumbe kwa Eliya, akisema, "Miungu na wanifanyie hivyo, na kuzidi, kwa maana kesho wakati kama huu nitaufanya uhai wako kama uhai wa mmoja wao."
sw.B: Basi Yezebeli akatuma mjumbe kwa Eliya kumwambia, "Miungu na wanitendee hivyo, na kuzidi, ikiwa kesho wakati kama huu sitakuwa nimeufanya uhai wako kama uhai wa mmoja wao."
sw.R: Basi Yezebeli akatuma mjumbe kwa Eliya na ujumbe huu: "Miungu na wanipe adhabu kali ikiwa kesho wakati kama huu sitakuwa nimekuua, kama ulivyowaua manabii wale!"

vi.L: Giê-sa-bên sai một sứ giả đến nói với Ê-li: "Nguyện các thần xử với ta như thế, và còn thêm nữa, nếu ngày mai vào giờ này ta không làm cho mạng sống ngươi giống như mạng sống của một trong những người ấy."
vi.B: Vậy Giê-sa-bên sai một sứ giả đến nói với Ê-li: "Nguyện các thần phạt ta nặng nề, nếu ngày mai vào giờ này ta không làm cho mạng sống ngươi giống như mạng sống của một người trong bọn họ."
vi.R: Vậy Giê-sa-bên sai một sứ giả đến báo cho Ê-li: "Nguyện các thần phạt ta thật nặng, nếu ngày mai vào giờ này ta không giết được ngươi, như ngươi đã giết các nhà tiên tri ấy!"

ko.L: 그러자 이세벨이 엘리야에게 사자를 보내어 말했다. "내일 이맘때 내가 네 목숨을 그들 가운데 하나의 목숨처럼 [만들지 못하면], 신들이 내게 이렇게 하고 또 더하여도 좋다."
ko.B: 그러자 이세벨이 엘리야에게 사자를 보내 말했다. "내일 이맘때까지 내가 네 목숨을 그 예언자들 가운데 하나의 목숨처럼 만들지 못하면, 신들이 내게 벌을 내리고 더 내려도 좋다."
ko.R: 그러자 이세벨이 엘리야에게 사자를 보내 이렇게 전했다. "네가 그 예언자들을 죽인 것처럼, 내가 내일 이맘때까지 너를 죽이지 못하면 신들이 내게 무서운 벌을 내려도 좋다!"

pt.L: E Jezabel enviou um mensageiro a Elias, dizendo: "Assim façam os deuses, e assim acrescentem, pois amanhã, por volta [desta] hora, farei a sua vida como a vida de um deles."
pt.B: Então Jezabel mandou um mensageiro dizer a Elias: "Que os deuses me tratem com toda a dureza, e mais ainda, se amanhã a esta hora eu não tiver feito com a sua vida o que foi feito com a vida de um deles."
pt.R: Então Jezabel mandou um mensageiro a Elias com este recado: "Que os deuses me castiguem duramente se amanhã a esta hora eu não tiver matado você, assim como você matou aqueles profetas!"

decisions.choice: thus may the gods do, and thus may they add: a self-curse
decisions.reason: This is the oath form used in 1 Samuel 3:17, 14:44, 20:13 and 25:22: the speaker calls punishment, and more, down on herself if she does not keep her word. The punishment is left unnamed. Here the verbs are plural, so Jezebel swears by "the gods", her own gods, not by the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: for by this time tomorrow I will make your life like theirs: what the oath binds her to
decisions.reason: After an oath the word "for" introduces what the speaker swears to do. Jezebel vows to kill Elijah within a day, as he killed her prophets (verse 1).

decisions.choice: a messenger: the same word as "angel" in verses 5 and 7
decisions.reason: The word means one who is sent with a message. Jezebel's messenger brings a threat of death; the LORD's messenger will bring Elijah food and life (verses 5-7).

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text has the threat only
alternatives: the Greek translation begins the message with "If you are Elijah, I am Jezebel"
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds a line at the start of Jezebel's message setting her name against his. The Hebrew text, which is followed here, does not have it.

decisions.choice: May the gods deal with me ever so severely if ...; May the gods punish me terribly if ...
decisions.reason: The oath is worded as in 1 Samuel 3:17, 14:44, 20:13 and 25:22, with "me" supplied because the oath is a curse on the speaker. "If ... I have not" states plainly what the oath binds her to.

decisions.choice: I have not killed you, just as you killed those prophets
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "make your life like the life of one of them" means.

decisions.choice: "Así me hagan los dioses, y así me añadan" (L); "Que los dioses me castiguen duramente, y aun más" (B); "Que los dioses me castiguen terriblemente" (R)
decisions.reason: The self-curse as the Samuel note sets for Spanish ("Así haga Dios ... y así le añada" / "Que Dios me castigue, y aun más"), with Jezebel's plural "gods" and a verb that agrees. Literal adds "me" and "si" so the oath reads in Spanish, as Samuel's Literal does.

decisions.choice: "Que les dieux fassent ainsi, et qu’ils y ajoutent" (L); "Que les dieux me traitent avec sévérité, et plus encore" (B); "Que les dieux me punissent sévèrement" (R)
alternatives: "Que les dieux me fassent ceci et pire encore"
decisions.reason: The self-curse as the Samuel terms note words it for God, with "les dieux" for Jezebel’s gods.

decisions.choice: Miungu na wanifanyie hivyo, na kuzidi
decisions.reason: Jezebel's oath follows the Swahili oath formula of Samuel ("Mungu anitendee hivyo, na kuzidi"), with "miungu" because she swears by her gods; Readable says plainly that she calls punishment on herself.

decisions.choice: "Nguyện các thần phạt ta nặng nề" (B, R); "xử với ta như thế, và còn thêm nữa" (L)
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's wording of the self-curse, here with "các thần", Jezebel's gods; she says "ta" and "ngươi" to the prophet she threatens.

decisions.choice: "신들이 내게 이렇게 하고 또 더하여도 좋다" (L), "신들이 내게 벌을 내리고 더 내려도 좋다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel wording of the self-curse, with "신들" in place of "하나님" because Jezebel swears by her gods. She threatens Elijah in 해라체.

decisions.choice: Assim façam os deuses, e assim acrescentem (L); Que os deuses me tratem com toda a dureza, e mais ainda (B); Que os deuses me castiguem duramente (R)
alternatives: Que os deuses façam comigo o que quiserem
decisions.reason: The self-curse (m1) keeps the Portuguese of 1 Samuel 20:13 level by level, with the plural "os deuses", Jezebel's own gods, as the subject. Jezebel speaks to Elijah with "você": the queen does not honour the prophet.

source.text: וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אֶל־נַפְשׁ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕א בְּאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּנַּ֥ח אֶֽת־נַעֲר֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he saw, and he arose and went for his life, and he came [to] Beersheba, which [belongs] to Judah, and he left his young man there.

en.L: And he saw [it], and he arose and went for his life, and he came to Beersheba, which [belongs] to Judah, and he left his young man there.
en.B: When Elijah saw how things stood, he got up and fled for his life. He reached Beersheba, in Judah, and left his servant there.
en.R: When Elijah saw what was happening, he got up and ran to save his life. He went to Beersheba, a town in Judah, far to the south, and left his servant there.

es.L: Y él [lo] vio, y se levantó y se fue para [salvar] su vida, y llegó a Beerseba, que [pertenece] a Judá, y dejó allí a su criado.
es.B: Cuando Elías vio cómo estaban las cosas, se levantó y huyó para salvar su vida. Llegó a Beerseba, en Judá, y dejó allí a su criado.
es.R: Cuando Elías vio lo que pasaba, se levantó y huyó para salvar su vida. Fue a Beerseba, una ciudad de Judá, muy al sur, y dejó allí a su criado.

fr.L: Et il vit [cela], il se leva et s’en alla pour sa vie, et il arriva à Beer-Shéba, qui [appartient] à Juda, et il laissa là son jeune homme.
fr.B: Voyant comment les choses tournaient, Élie se leva et s’enfuit pour sauver sa vie. Il arriva à Beer-Shéba, en Juda, et il y laissa son serviteur.
fr.R: Quand Élie a vu ce qui se passait, il s’est levé et il s’est enfui pour sauver sa vie. Il est allé à Beer-Shéba, une ville de Juda, tout au sud, et il y a laissé son serviteur.

sw.L: Akaona, akainuka akaenda kwa ajili ya uhai wake, akafika Beer-sheba, ulio [mji] wa Yuda, akamwacha kijana wake huko.
sw.B: Eliya alipoona hali ilivyokuwa, aliinuka akakimbia kuokoa maisha yake. Akafika Beer-sheba katika Yuda, akamwacha mtumishi wake huko.
sw.R: Eliya alipoona yaliyokuwa yakitokea, aliinuka akakimbia ili kuokoa maisha yake. Akaenda Beer-sheba, mji wa Yuda ulio mbali kusini, akamwacha mtumishi wake huko.

vi.L: Ông thấy [vậy], liền đứng dậy đi để cứu mạng mình; ông đến Bê-e-Sê-ba, thuộc Giu-đa, và để người đầy tớ trẻ của mình lại đó.
vi.B: Thấy vậy, Ê-li đứng dậy trốn đi để giữ mạng sống mình. Ông đến Bê-e-Sê-ba thuộc Giu-đa và để người đầy tớ lại đó.
vi.R: Thấy tình thế như vậy, Ê-li đứng dậy chạy trốn để giữ mạng sống. Ông đến Bê-e-Sê-ba, một thành của Giu-đa ở tận miền nam, và để người đầy tớ ở lại đó.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 [그것을] 보고, 일어나 자기 목숨을 위해 떠나 유다에 속한 브엘세바에 이르렀다. 그리고 그가 거기에 그의 젊은이를 남겨 두었다.
ko.B: 엘리야는 형편을 보고 일어나 목숨을 건지려고 도망했다. 그는 유다 땅 브엘세바에 이르러 자기 종을 거기에 남겨 두었다.
ko.R: 엘리야는 일이 어떻게 되어 가는지 보고 목숨을 건지려고 도망쳤다. 그는 남쪽 끝 유다 땅의 브엘세바라는 성읍으로 갔다. 그리고 자기 종을 거기에 남겨 두었다.

pt.L: E ele viu [isso], e se levantou, e partiu para [salvar] a sua vida, e chegou a Berseba, que [pertence] a Judá, e deixou ali o seu moço.
pt.B: Quando Elias viu como estavam as coisas, levantou-se e fugiu para salvar a vida. Chegou a Berseba, em Judá, e deixou ali o seu servo.
pt.R: Quando Elias viu o que estava acontecendo, levantou-se e fugiu para salvar a vida. Ele foi até Berseba, uma cidade de Judá, bem no sul, e deixou ali o seu servo.

decisions.choice: he saw, as the vowels of the Hebrew text read
alternatives: he was afraid (the same consonants with different vowels, as some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient translations read)
decisions.reason: The written consonants can be read as "he saw" or "he was afraid". The standard Hebrew text points them as "he saw", which is followed here: Elijah sees his danger. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek, Syriac and Latin translations read "he was afraid". Either way he runs for his life.

decisions.choice: went for his life: fled to save himself
decisions.reason: To go "for one's life" (2 Kings 7:7) is to flee to stay alive.

decisions.choice: Beersheba, which belongs to Judah: outside Ahab's kingdom
decisions.reason: Beersheba lay at the far south of the land ("from Dan to Beersheba", 1 Samuel 3:20). Belonging to Judah, it was in the southern kingdom, out of reach of Ahab and Jezebel, who ruled Israel in the north.

decisions.choice: his young man: his servant or attendant
decisions.reason: The word means a young man and is often used of a personal attendant (Genesis 22:3; Judges 7:10). Elijah goes on alone.

decisions.choice: Elijah saw how things stood; saw what was happening
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he saw" with no object. Balanced and Readable supply what he saw: the danger Jezebel's message showed him.

decisions.choice: a town in Judah, far to the south
decisions.reason: Readable adds where Beersheba lay so the reader can see how far Elijah fled.

decisions.choice: "Beerseba"
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's form ("desde Dan hasta Beerseba").

source.text: וְהֽוּא־הָלַ֤ךְ בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ י֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיֵּ֕שֶׁב תַּ֖חַת רֹ֣תֶם אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ לָמ֔וּת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀רַ֗ב עַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ קַ֣ח נַפְשִׁ֔י כִּֽי־לֹא־ט֥וֹב אָנֹכִ֖י מֵאֲבֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went in the wilderness a journey of a day, and came and sat under a broom tree, one, and he asked his life to die, and said, Enough! Now, Yahweh, take my life, for not good [am] I more than my fathers.

en.L: And he himself went into the wilderness a day's journey, and he came and sat under a certain broom tree; and he asked for himself that he might die, and said, "[It is] enough! Now, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, take my life, for I [am] not better than my fathers."
en.B: But he himself went on a day's journey into the wilderness. He came to a broom tree and sat down under it, and he prayed that he might die. "It is enough," he said. "Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, take my life, for I am no better than my {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}."
en.R: Then Elijah walked on alone into the desert for a whole day. He sat down under a broom bush and asked to die. "I have had enough, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}," he said. "Take my life now. I am no better than my {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}."

es.L: Y él mismo se fue al desierto un día de camino, y llegó y se sentó debajo de una retama; y pidió para sí la muerte, y dijo: «¡Basta ya! Ahora, oh {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, quítame la vida, porque no [soy] yo mejor que mis padres».
es.B: Pero él siguió un día de camino por el desierto. Llegó a una retama y se sentó debajo de ella, y pidió morirse. «¡Ya basta!», dijo. «Ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, quítame la vida, porque no soy mejor que mis antepasados».
es.R: Luego Elías caminó solo por el desierto todo un día. Se sentó debajo de una retama y pidió morirse. «Ya no puedo más, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}», dijo. «Quítame la vida ahora. No soy mejor que mis antepasados».

fr.L: Et lui-même alla dans le désert une journée de chemin, et il vint s’asseoir sous un genêt ; et il demanda pour lui-même de mourir, et dit : « C’[est] assez ! Maintenant, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, prends ma vie, car je ne [suis] pas meilleur que mes pères. »
fr.B: Mais lui-même s’avança dans le désert à une journée de marche. Il arriva près d’un genêt, s’assit dessous et demanda la mort. « C’est assez, dit-il. Maintenant, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, prends ma vie, car je ne vaux pas mieux que mes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. »
fr.R: Ensuite Élie a marché seul dans le désert pendant toute une journée. Il s’est assis sous un buisson de genêt et il a demandé à mourir. « J’en ai assez, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, a-t-il dit. Prends ma vie maintenant. Je ne vaux pas mieux que mes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. »

sw.L: Lakini yeye mwenyewe akaenda jangwani mwendo wa siku moja, akafika akaketi chini ya mretemu mmoja; akajiombea kufa, akasema, "Imetosha! Sasa, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uchukue uhai wangu, kwa maana mimi si bora kuliko baba zangu."
sw.B: Lakini yeye mwenyewe akaendelea mwendo wa siku moja jangwani. Akafika kwenye mretemu, akaketi chini yake, akaomba afe. Akasema, "Imetosha. Sasa, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, chukua uhai wangu, kwa maana mimi si bora kuliko babu zangu."
sw.R: Kisha Eliya akatembea peke yake jangwani kwa siku nzima. Akaketi chini ya kichaka cha mretemu, akaomba afe. Akasema, "Nimechoka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Chukua uhai wangu sasa. Mimi si bora kuliko babu zangu."

vi.L: Còn chính ông đi vào hoang mạc một ngày đường, đến ngồi dưới một cây giếng giêng, và xin cho mình được chết, rằng: "Đủ rồi! Bây giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin lấy mạng sống con đi, vì con chẳng hơn gì tổ phụ con."
vi.B: Còn chính ông đi tiếp một ngày đường vào hoang mạc. Ông đến ngồi dưới một cây giếng giêng và cầu xin cho mình được chết. Ông nói: "Đủ rồi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Bây giờ xin lấy mạng sống con đi, vì con chẳng hơn gì tổ tiên con."
vi.R: Rồi Ê-li đi một mình vào hoang mạc suốt một ngày. Ông ngồi xuống dưới một bụi cây giếng giêng và xin được chết. Ông nói: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con chịu hết nổi rồi. Xin lấy mạng sống con ngay bây giờ. Con chẳng hơn gì tổ tiên con."

ko.L: 그리고 그는 광야로 하룻길을 가서, 한 로뎀 나무 아래에 와서 앉았다. 그리고 그는 자기가 죽기를 구하며 말했다. "넉넉합니다! 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제 목숨을 거두어 주십시오. 저는 제 조상들보다 낫지 않습니다."
ko.B: 그러나 그는 혼자서 광야로 하룻길을 들어갔다. 그는 로뎀 나무 아래에 와서 앉아 죽기를 구하며 말했다. "이제 그만하면 되었습니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 이제 제 목숨을 거두어 주십시오. 저는 제 조상들보다 나을 것이 없습니다."
ko.R: 그리고 엘리야는 혼자서 하루 종일 광야로 걸어 들어갔다. 그는 덤불 아래에 앉아 죽기를 구했다. 그가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 이제 더는 못 하겠습니다. 지금 제 목숨을 거두어 주십시오. 저는 제 조상들보다 나을 것이 없습니다."

pt.L: E ele mesmo foi para o deserto o caminho de um dia, e chegou e se sentou debaixo de uma giesta; e pediu para si a morte, e disse: "Basta! Agora, ó {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, toma a minha vida, pois eu não [sou] melhor do que os meus pais."
pt.B: Mas ele mesmo seguiu deserto adentro, um dia de caminhada. Chegou a uma giesta, sentou-se debaixo dela e pediu a morte. "Basta", disse ele. "Agora, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, tira a minha vida, pois não sou melhor do que os meus {{gender:antepassados|pais}}."
pt.R: Depois Elias andou sozinho pelo deserto um dia inteiro. Ele se sentou debaixo de uma moita de giesta e pediu para morrer. "Para mim chega, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}", disse ele. "Tira agora a minha vida. Não sou melhor do que os meus {{gender:antepassados|pais}}."

decisions.choice: broom tree: a desert shrub
decisions.reason: The broom is a bush of the southern wilderness that can grow to the height of a small tree and gives a little shade. Its roots were burned for charcoal (Psalm 120:4; Job 30:4).

decisions.choice: asked his life to die: asked that he might die
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Jonah's wish to die (Jonah 4:8).

decisions.choice: for I am not better than my fathers: why he wants to die
alternatives: for I am no better than my ancestors, who also failed
for I am no better than my ancestors, who all died
decisions.reason: Elijah may mean that he has done no better than those before him at turning Israel back to the LORD, or simply that he is mortal like them and is ready to go the same way. The words do not say which.

decisions.choice: take my life: echoes Moses' prayer
decisions.reason: Moses too, worn out by the people, asked the LORD to kill him (Numbers 11:15). Elijah's journey to Horeb (verse 8) will make the likeness to Moses clearer.

decisions.choice: LORD, without the article
decisions.reason: When the name is used to call on God directly, English writes "LORD" without "the".

decisions.choice: desert; broom bush
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the wilderness and for the low tree.

decisions.choice: "una retama"
decisions.reason: The desert broom bush; Spanish "retama" names the same plant.

decisions.choice: "mis antepasados", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "antepasados" already takes in men and women, so the English gender span has no Spanish counterpart, as the Samuel drafts settle.

decisions.choice: "un genêt" (L, B); "un buisson de genêt" (R)
decisions.reason: French has the plant’s own name, the broom of the desert; Readable says it was a bush.

decisions.choice: mretemu
decisions.reason: The broom tree is a desert shrub; "mretemu" is its Swahili name, and Readable adds "kichaka" (bush), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: babu zangu, without a gender span
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on "ancestors"; Swahili "babu" already covers forefathers of both sexes, so there is no span, as the Samuel note sets for ancestors.

decisions.choice: "cây giếng giêng" for the broom tree
decisions.reason: The desert broom has a long-used Vietnamese Bible name; Readable says "bụi cây", as the English Readable says "bush".

decisions.choice: no gender span for "tổ phụ / tổ tiên"
decisions.reason: As in Samuel, "tổ phụ" (L) and "tổ tiên" (B, R) already include both sexes, so the English gender setting has no second wording.

decisions.choice: "로뎀 나무" (L, B), "덤불" (R)
decisions.reason: "로뎀 나무" is the familiar Korean name of the desert broom; Readable says only that it was a bush, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Elijah prays in 합쇼체 with "저"
decisions.reason: As in the Korean style guide, people praying speak to God in 합쇼체; his complaint stays a prayer.

decisions.choice: uma giesta (L, B); uma moita de giesta (R)
decisions.reason: The desert shrub (m1) is the broom, "giesta" in Portuguese, the plant the English names; "zimbro", familiar from older Portuguese Bibles, is the juniper, a different plant. Readable says "moita", a bush, as the English Readable says "broom bush". Elijah prays with "tu" and calls on God with "SENHOR" without the article ("tira a minha vida").

decisions.choice: {{gender:antepassados|pais}}
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable offer an inclusive default with the traditional word as the alternative: "antepassados" takes in mothers and fathers, while plural "pais" here means the forefathers. Literal keeps "pais" without a setting, as the English Literal keeps "fathers".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙ וַיִּישַׁ֔ן תַּ֖חַת רֹ֣תֶם אֶחָ֑ד וְהִנֵּֽה־זֶ֤ה מַלְאָךְ֙ נֹגֵ֣עַ בּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ ק֥וּם אֱכֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he lay down and slept under a broom tree, one, and look! this, an angel touching him, and he said to him, Arise, eat.

en.L: And he lay down and slept under a certain broom tree; and look, an angel [was] touching him, and he said to him, "Arise, eat."
en.B: Then he lay down and slept under the broom tree. And all at once an angel touched him and said to him, "Get up and eat."
en.R: Then he lay down under the bush and went to sleep. All at once an angel touched him. "Get up and eat!" the angel said.

es.L: Y se acostó y se durmió debajo de una retama; y he aquí que un ángel lo tocaba, y le dijo: «Levántate, come».
es.B: Luego se acostó y se durmió debajo de la retama. De pronto un ángel lo tocó y le dijo: «Levántate y come».
es.R: Luego se acostó debajo de la retama y se durmió. De pronto un ángel lo tocó. «¡Levántate y come!», le dijo el ángel.

fr.L: Et il se coucha et s’endormit sous un genêt ; et voici, un ange le touchait, et il lui dit : « Lève-toi, mange. »
fr.B: Puis il se coucha et s’endormit sous le genêt. Et voici qu’un ange le toucha et lui dit : « Lève-toi et mange. »
fr.R: Ensuite il s’est couché sous le buisson et il s’est endormi. Tout à coup, un ange l’a touché. « Lève-toi et mange ! » lui a dit l’ange.

sw.L: Akalala akapata usingizi chini ya mretemu mmoja; na tazama, malaika [alikuwa] akimgusa, akamwambia, "Inuka, ule."
sw.B: Kisha akajilaza akalala chini ya ule mretemu. Ghafla malaika akamgusa, akamwambia, "Inuka ule."
sw.R: Kisha akajilaza chini ya kichaka, akapata usingizi. Ghafla malaika akamgusa. Malaika akasema, "Inuka ule!"

vi.L: Ông nằm xuống và ngủ dưới một cây giếng giêng; kìa, một thiên sứ chạm đến ông và nói với ông: "Hãy dậy mà ăn."
vi.B: Rồi ông nằm xuống ngủ dưới cây giếng giêng. Thình lình một thiên sứ chạm đến ông và bảo: "Hãy dậy mà ăn."
vi.R: Rồi ông nằm xuống dưới bụi cây và ngủ thiếp đi. Thình lình một thiên sứ chạm vào ông và nói: "Hãy dậy mà ăn!"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 한 로뎀 나무 아래에 누워 잠이 들었다. 그런데 보라, 천사가 그를 어루만지며 그에게 말했다. "일어나 먹어라."
ko.B: 그러고는 로뎀 나무 아래에 누워 잠이 들었다. 그때 갑자기 천사가 그를 어루만지며 말했다. "일어나 먹어라."
ko.R: 그러고는 덤불 아래에 누워 잠이 들었다. 그런데 갑자기 천사가 그를 어루만졌다. 천사가 말했다. "일어나 먹어라!"

pt.L: E ele se deitou e dormiu debaixo de uma giesta; e eis que um anjo o tocava e lhe disse: "Levanta-te, come."
pt.B: Então ele se deitou e dormiu debaixo da giesta. De repente, um anjo o tocou e lhe disse: "Levanta-te e come."
pt.R: Depois ele se deitou debaixo da moita e dormiu. De repente, um anjo o tocou. "Levanta-te e come!", disse o anjo.

decisions.choice: an angel: a messenger from God
decisions.reason: The word is the same as Jezebel's "messenger" in verse 2. Verse 7 says who sent this one: he is "the angel of the LORD".

decisions.choice: look, an angel touching him: a sudden surprise
decisions.reason: The word "look" with the participle shows the scene through Elijah's eyes as he wakes.

decisions.choice: the broom tree
decisions.reason: The tree was introduced in verse 4; Balanced points back to it.

decisions.choice: tu (the angel to Elijah): "Levanta-te e come"
decisions.reason: The angel is the LORD's own messenger (verse 7, m1) and speaks for him, so he says "tu" to Elijah, as God speaks to one person throughout the Old Testament.

source.text: וַיַּבֵּ֕ט וְהִנֵּ֧ה מְרַאֲשֹׁתָ֛יו עֻגַ֥ת רְצָפִ֖ים וְצַפַּ֣חַת מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֣אכַל וַיֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וַיָּ֖שָׁב וַיִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he looked, and look! at his head [was] a cake of hot stones and a jar of water; and he ate and drank, and he returned and lay down.

en.L: And he looked, and look, at his head [was] a cake [baked on] hot stones and a jar of water. And he ate and drank, and lay down again.
en.B: He looked, and there by his head was a loaf baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He ate and drank, and then lay down again.
en.R: He looked around. Next to his head was some bread baked on hot stones, and a jar of water. So he ate and drank, and then he lay down again.

es.L: Y miró, y he aquí que a su cabecera [había] una torta [cocida sobre] piedras calientes y una jarra de agua. Y comió y bebió, y volvió a acostarse.
es.B: Miró, y junto a su cabeza había un pan cocido sobre piedras calientes y una jarra de agua. Comió y bebió, y volvió a acostarse.
es.R: Miró a su alrededor. Junto a su cabeza había un pan cocido sobre piedras calientes, y una jarra de agua. Así que comió y bebió, y luego se volvió a acostar.

fr.L: Et il regarda, et voici, à son chevet [il y avait] une galette [cuite sur des] pierres chaudes et une cruche d’eau. Et il mangea et but, et se recoucha.
fr.B: Il regarda, et voici qu’il y avait à son chevet une galette cuite sur des pierres chaudes et une cruche d’eau. Il mangea et but, puis se recoucha.
fr.R: Il a regardé autour de lui. À côté de sa tête, il y avait du pain cuit sur des pierres chaudes et une cruche d’eau. Il a mangé et bu, puis il s’est recouché.

sw.L: Akatazama, na tazama, kichwani pake [palikuwa na] mkate [uliookwa juu ya] mawe ya moto na gudulia la maji. Akala, akanywa, akalala tena.
sw.B: Akatazama, na hapo karibu na kichwa chake palikuwa na mkate uliookwa juu ya mawe ya moto na gudulia la maji. Akala, akanywa, kisha akalala tena.
sw.R: Akatazama huku na huku. Karibu na kichwa chake palikuwa na mkate uliookwa juu ya mawe ya moto, na gudulia la maji. Basi akala, akanywa, kisha akalala tena.

vi.L: Ông nhìn, kìa, ở đầu ông có một cái bánh [nướng trên] đá nóng và một bình nước. Ông ăn và uống, rồi lại nằm xuống.
vi.B: Ông nhìn, thấy ngay bên đầu mình có một cái bánh nướng trên đá nóng và một bình nước. Ông ăn uống rồi lại nằm xuống.
vi.R: Ông nhìn quanh. Bên cạnh đầu ông có một ít bánh nướng trên đá nóng và một bình nước. Vậy ông ăn uống, rồi lại nằm xuống.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 보니, 보라, 그의 머리맡에 뜨거운 돌에 [구운] 빵과 물 한 병이 있었다. 그리고 그가 먹고 마시고 다시 누웠다.
ko.B: 그가 둘러보니, 머리맡에 뜨거운 돌에 구운 빵과 물 한 병이 놓여 있었다. 그는 먹고 마신 뒤에 다시 누웠다.
ko.R: 그가 둘러보니, 머리맡에 뜨거운 돌에 구운 빵과 물 한 병이 있었다. 그래서 그는 먹고 마셨다. 그리고 다시 누웠다.

pt.L: E ele olhou, e eis que, à sua cabeceira, [havia] um pão [assado sobre] pedras quentes e uma jarra de água. E ele comeu e bebeu, e voltou a deitar-se.
pt.B: Ele olhou, e ali, junto à sua cabeça, havia um pão assado sobre pedras quentes e uma jarra de água. Ele comeu e bebeu, e depois se deitou de novo.
pt.R: Ele olhou em volta. Ao lado da sua cabeça havia um pão assado sobre pedras quentes e uma jarra de água. Então ele comeu e bebeu, e depois se deitou de novo.

decisions.choice: a cake of hot stones: a round flat loaf baked on heated stones
decisions.reason: Bread was often baked by laying the dough on stones heated in the fire (compare Genesis 18:6). The loaf here seems to have been made ready for Elijah while he slept.

decisions.choice: a jar: a small pottery water jug
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the water jar David took from beside the sleeping Saul's head (1 Samuel 26:11-12).

decisions.choice: he returned and lay down: he lay down again
decisions.reason: The verb "return" before another verb often means doing it again.

decisions.choice: [baked on]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "a cake of hot stones"; Literal brackets the words that show what the phrase means.

decisions.choice: uma jarra de água
decisions.reason: The small water jug (m2) is the same Hebrew word as the widow's oil jug (17:12), so Portuguese keeps "jarra" for both; "cântaro" is kept for the large jars carried on the shoulder (18:34).

source.text: וַיָּשָׁב֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֤ה׀שֵׁנִית֙ וַיִּגַּע־בּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר ק֣וּם אֱכֹ֑ל כִּ֛י רַ֥ב מִמְּךָ֖ הַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned [the] angel of Yahweh a second [time] and touched him, and said, Arise, eat, for too great for you [is] the journey.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came back a second time and touched him and said, "Arise, eat, for the journey [is] too great for you."
en.B: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came back a second time, touched him and said, "Get up and eat, for the journey is too much for you."
en.R: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came back a second time. He touched Elijah and said, "Get up and eat! The trip ahead of you is too long for you."

es.L: Y el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} volvió por segunda vez y lo tocó y dijo: «Levántate, come, porque el camino [es] demasiado largo para ti».
es.B: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} volvió por segunda vez, lo tocó y le dijo: «Levántate y come, porque el viaje es demasiado largo para ti».
es.R: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} volvió por segunda vez. Tocó a Elías y le dijo: «¡Levántate y come! El viaje que tienes por delante es demasiado largo para ti».

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} revint une deuxième fois, le toucha et dit : « Lève-toi, mange, car le chemin [est] trop long pour toi. »
fr.B: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} revint une deuxième fois, le toucha et lui dit : « Lève-toi et mange, car le chemin est trop long pour toi. »
fr.R: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est revenu une deuxième fois. Il a touché Élie et il lui a dit : « Lève-toi et mange ! Le voyage qui t’attend est trop long pour toi. »

sw.L: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akarudi mara ya pili, akamgusa, akasema, "Inuka, ule, kwa maana safari [ni] ndefu mno kwako."
sw.B: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akarudi mara ya pili, akamgusa, akasema, "Inuka ule, kwa maana safari ni ndefu mno kwako."
sw.R: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akarudi mara ya pili. Akamgusa Eliya, akasema, "Inuka ule! Safari iliyo mbele yako ni ndefu mno kwako."

vi.L: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trở lại lần thứ hai, chạm đến ông và nói: "Hãy dậy mà ăn, vì đường đi quá xa cho ngươi."
vi.B: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trở lại lần thứ hai, chạm đến ông và nói: "Hãy dậy mà ăn, vì chặng đường còn quá sức con."
vi.R: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trở lại lần thứ hai. Thiên sứ chạm vào Ê-li và nói: "Hãy dậy mà ăn! Chặng đường phía trước còn quá dài đối với con."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 두 번째로 다시 와서 그를 어루만지며 말했다. "일어나 먹어라. 네가 갈 길이 너에게 너무 멀다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 다시 와서 두 번째로 그를 어루만지며 말했다. "일어나 먹어라. 갈 길이 너에게는 너무 멀다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 두 번째로 다시 왔다. 그는 엘리야를 어루만지며 말했다. "일어나 먹어라! 앞으로 갈 길이 너에게 너무 멀다."

pt.L: E o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} voltou uma segunda vez, e o tocou, e disse: "Levanta-te, come, porque o caminho [é] longo demais para ti."
pt.B: O anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} voltou pela segunda vez, tocou-o e disse: "Levanta-te e come, pois a viagem é longa demais para ti."
pt.R: O anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} voltou pela segunda vez. Ele tocou Elias e disse: "Levanta-te e come! A viagem que tens pela frente é longa demais para ti."

decisions.choice: the angel of Yahweh: the messenger the LORD has sent
decisions.reason: The narrator now names the angel of verse 5 as the LORD's own messenger (see Judges 2:1; 6:11). The LORD answers Elijah's prayer to die not with death but with food and strength.

decisions.choice: for the journey is too great for you: the journey still ahead
decisions.reason: Elijah has not said he is going anywhere; the angel speaks of a journey still to come, the one to Horeb (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the trip ahead of you
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the journey is still to come.

decisions.choice: "el ángel del SEÑOR"
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch note sets for Spanish.

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD speaks as God does: "ngươi" (L), "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The angel speaks for the LORD, so he addresses Elijah as God does in this chapter.

source.text: וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֹּ֣אכַל וַיִּשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּכֹ֣חַ׀הָאֲכִילָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה עַ֛ד הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he arose and ate and drank, and went in [the] strength of the food, that, forty day[s] and forty night[s] to [the] mountain of God, Horeb.

en.L: And he arose and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to the mountain of God, Horeb.
en.B: So he got up, ate and drank, and in the strength of that food he walked forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
en.R: So Elijah got up and ate and drank. That food gave him strength to walk for forty days and forty nights. He walked all the way to Horeb, the mountain of God.

es.L: Y se levantó y comió y bebió, y anduvo con la fuerza de aquella comida cuarenta días y cuarenta noches hasta el monte de Dios, Horeb.
es.B: Así que se levantó, comió y bebió, y con la fuerza de aquella comida caminó cuarenta días y cuarenta noches hasta Horeb, el monte de Dios.
es.R: Así que Elías se levantó, comió y bebió. Esa comida le dio fuerzas para caminar durante cuarenta días y cuarenta noches. Caminó todo el trayecto hasta Horeb, el monte de Dios.

fr.L: Et il se leva, mangea et but, et il marcha avec la force de cette nourriture quarante jours et quarante nuits jusqu’à la montagne de Dieu, l’Horeb.
fr.B: Il se leva donc, mangea et but, et avec la force que lui donna cette nourriture il marcha quarante jours et quarante nuits jusqu’à l’Horeb, la montagne de Dieu.
fr.R: Élie s’est donc levé, il a mangé et il a bu. Cette nourriture lui a donné la force de marcher pendant quarante jours et quarante nuits. Il a marché jusqu’à l’Horeb, la montagne de Dieu.

sw.L: Akainuka, akala, akanywa, akaenda kwa nguvu ya chakula kile siku arobaini mchana na usiku mpaka mlima wa Mungu, Horebu.
sw.B: Basi akainuka, akala, akanywa, na kwa nguvu ya chakula kile akatembea siku arobaini mchana na usiku mpaka Horebu, mlima wa Mungu.
sw.R: Basi Eliya akainuka, akala, akanywa. Chakula kile kilimpa nguvu za kutembea siku arobaini mchana na usiku. Akatembea mpaka Horebu, mlima wa Mungu.

vi.L: Ông đứng dậy ăn và uống, rồi nhờ sức của thức ăn ấy mà đi bốn mươi ngày bốn mươi đêm đến núi của Đức Chúa Trời là Hô-rếp.
vi.B: Vậy ông dậy ăn uống, rồi nhờ sức của thức ăn ấy, ông đi bốn mươi ngày bốn mươi đêm đến Hô-rếp, núi của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Vậy Ê-li dậy ăn uống. Thức ăn ấy cho ông sức để đi bốn mươi ngày bốn mươi đêm. Ông đi bộ suốt đến Hô-rếp, núi của Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 일어나 먹고 마시고, 그 음식의 힘으로 사십 일 낮과 사십 일 밤을 걸어 하나님의 산 호렙에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 그는 일어나 먹고 마셨다. 그리고 그 음식에서 얻은 힘으로 사십 일 낮과 밤을 걸어 하나님의 산 호렙에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 그래서 엘리야는 일어나 먹고 마셨다. 그 음식이 힘이 되어 그는 사십 일 동안 밤낮으로 걸었다. 그는 하나님의 산인 호렙까지 걸어갔다.

pt.L: E ele se levantou, e comeu, e bebeu, e foi na força daquela comida quarenta dias e quarenta noites até o monte de Deus, Horebe.
pt.B: Então ele se levantou, comeu e bebeu e, com a força daquela comida, caminhou quarenta dias e quarenta noites até Horebe, o monte de Deus.
pt.R: Então Elias se levantou, comeu e bebeu. Aquela comida lhe deu força para caminhar quarenta dias e quarenta noites. Ele andou até chegar a Horebe, o monte de Deus.

decisions.choice: forty days and forty nights: as Moses on the mountain
decisions.reason: Moses was on the mountain with the LORD forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24:18), and the second time he neither ate nor drank (Exodus 34:28; Deuteronomy 9:9, 18). Elijah, kept alive by the food God gave, makes his own forty days' journey to the same mountain.

decisions.choice: Horeb, the mountain of God: the mountain also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Horeb is the name Deuteronomy and Exodus 3:1 use for the mountain where the LORD met Moses and gave the covenant (Exodus 3:1; Deuteronomy 5:2). Elijah, the defender of that covenant (verse 10), goes back to where it began.

decisions.choice: forty days: a long journey, more than the distance needs
decisions.reason: From Beersheba to the traditional site of Sinai is about two weeks' walk. The forty days may include wandering, or the number may be chosen to match Moses' forty days; the text gives no route.

decisions.choice: to Horeb, the mountain of God
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the name first, as English usually does.

decisions.choice: siku arobaini mchana na usiku
decisions.reason: Swahili says "forty days and forty nights" in its usual way, "siku arobaini mchana na usiku", at every level.

decisions.choice: "Hô-rếp"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant form of Horeb.

decisions.choice: o monte de Deus, Horebe (L); Horebe, o monte de Deus (B, R)
decisions.reason: The mountain (m2) keeps the name and the words of Exodus 3:1 in Portuguese, "Horebe, o monte de Deus" at Balanced and Readable and in the Hebrew order at Literal, so the reader sees Elijah come to the mountain where the LORD met Moses.

source.text: וַיָּבֹא־שָׁ֥ם אֶל־הַמְּעָרָ֖ה וַיָּ֣לֶן שָׁ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מַה־לְּךָ֥ פֹ֖ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he came there to the cave and spent the night there; and look! [the] word of Yahweh [was] to him, and he said to him, What to you here, Elijah?

en.L: And he came there to the cave and spent the night there. And look, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [came] to him, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "What [is it] to you here, Elijah?"
en.B: There he came to the cave and spent the night in it. Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
en.R: When he got there, he went into a cave and spent the night. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to him. He asked, "Elijah, what are you doing here?"

es.L: Y llegó allí a la cueva y pasó allí la noche. Y he aquí que la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [vino] a él, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dijo: «¿Qué [haces] tú aquí, Elías?».
es.B: Allí llegó a la cueva y pasó la noche en ella. Entonces la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a él: «¿Qué haces aquí, Elías?».
es.R: Cuando llegó allí, entró en una cueva y pasó la noche. Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le habló. Le preguntó: «Elías, ¿qué haces aquí?».

fr.L: Et il arriva là, à la grotte, et il y passa la nuit. Et voici, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [vint] à lui, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Qu’as-tu [à faire] ici, Élie ? »
fr.B: Arrivé là, il entra dans la grotte et y passa la nuit. Alors la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui fut adressée : « Que fais-tu ici, Élie ? »
fr.R: Quand il est arrivé là-bas, il est entré dans une grotte et il y a passé la nuit. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a parlé. Il lui a demandé : « Élie, que fais-tu ici ? »

sw.L: Akafika huko kwenye pango, akalala huko usiku. Na tazama, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [likamjia], {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akamwambia, "Una nini hapa, Eliya?"
sw.B: Huko akafika kwenye pango, akalala humo usiku. Ndipo neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likamjia: "Unafanya nini hapa, Eliya?"
sw.R: Alipofika huko, akaingia katika pango, akalala humo usiku. Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema naye. Akamwuliza, "Eliya, unafanya nini hapa?"

vi.L: Tại đó ông vào hang và qua đêm ở đó. Kìa, lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [đến] với ông, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với ông: "Ngươi làm gì ở đây, hỡi Ê-li?"
vi.B: Đến nơi, ông vào hang và qua đêm trong đó. Bấy giờ lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với ông: "Ê-li, con làm gì ở đây?"
vi.R: Đến nơi, ông vào một cái hang và ngủ qua đêm. Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với ông. Ngài hỏi: "Ê-li, con đang làm gì ở đây?"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 거기서 그 굴에 들어가 거기서 밤을 지냈다. 그런데 보라, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 그에게 [임하여] 그분께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "엘리야야, 여기서 너에게 무슨 [일이냐]?"
ko.B: 그는 거기에 이르러 그 굴에 들어가 밤을 지냈다. 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 그에게 임했다. "엘리야야, 너는 여기서 무엇을 하고 있느냐?"
ko.R: 그곳에 이르자 엘리야는 굴에 들어가서 밤을 지냈다. 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. 그분께서 물으셨다. "엘리야야, 너는 여기서 무엇을 하고 있느냐?"

pt.L: E ele chegou ali à caverna e passou a noite ali. E eis que a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} [veio] a ele, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe disse: "Que [há] para ti aqui, Elias?"
pt.B: Ali ele entrou na caverna e passou a noite nela. Então a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a ele: "Que fazes aqui, Elias?"
pt.R: Quando chegou lá, ele entrou numa caverna e passou a noite. Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou com ele e perguntou: "Elias, o que estás fazendo aqui?"

decisions.choice: the cave: a particular cave on the mountain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "the cave", as if it were a place already known. It may recall the cleft in the rock where the LORD put Moses as his glory passed by (Exodus 33:21-22), though a different word is used there.

decisions.choice: what to you here: what are you doing here?
decisions.reason: The question asks what has brought Elijah here and what he wants. It is asked again, in the same words, in verse 13.

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came to him: the LORD spoke to him
decisions.reason: This is the usual way of saying that the LORD gave a prophet a message (17:2, 8; 18:1).

decisions.choice: the LORD spoke to him. He asked
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that it was the LORD who spoke, and gives his words as a question he asked.

decisions.choice: What are you doing here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom "what to you here?" is given as the natural question.

decisions.choice: "¿Qué [haces] tú aquí?" (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "What to you here?" cannot stand word for word in Spanish; Literal supplies the verb in brackets.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ קַנֹּ֨א קִנֵּ֜אתִי לַיהוָ֣ה׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֗וֹת כִּֽי־עָזְב֤וּ בְרִֽיתְךָ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתֶ֣יךָ הָרָ֔סוּ וְאֶת־נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ הָרְג֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב וָֽאִוָּתֵ֤ר אֲנִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י וַיְבַקְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Being zealous I have been zealous for Yahweh God of hosts, for have forsaken your covenant [the] sons of Israel; your altars they have torn down, and your prophets they have killed with the sword; and am left I, I alone, and they seek my life to take it.

en.L: And he said, "I have been very zealous for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts, for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant; they have torn down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, and they have killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets with the sword. And I am left, I alone, and they seek my life, to take it."
en.B: He answered, "I have been very zealous for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant. They have torn down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets to the sword. I alone am left, and now they are seeking to take my life."
en.R: Elijah answered, "I have worked with all my heart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies. But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant. They have torn down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars and killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets with swords. I am the only one left, and now they want to kill me too."

es.L: Y él dijo: «He sentido un vivo celo por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los ejércitos, porque los hijos de Israel han abandonado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pacto; han derribado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares y han matado a espada a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} profetas. Y he quedado yo, yo solo, y buscan mi vida para quitármela».
es.B: Él respondió: «He sentido un gran celo por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los Ejércitos, porque los israelitas han abandonado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pacto. Han derribado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares y han pasado a espada a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} profetas. Solo quedo yo, y ahora me buscan para quitarme la vida».
es.R: Elías respondió: «He trabajado con todo mi corazón para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los Ejércitos. Pero los israelitas se han apartado de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pacto. Han derribado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares y han matado a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} profetas a espada. Soy el único que queda, y ahora quieren matarme a mí también».

fr.L: Et il dit : « J’ai été plein de zèle, plein de zèle pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées, car les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ont abandonné {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} alliance ; ils ont démoli {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels, et ils ont tué {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} prophètes par l’épée. Et je suis resté, moi seul, et ils cherchent ma vie pour me l’ôter. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « J’ai été rempli de zèle pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées, parce que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont abandonné {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} alliance. Ils ont démoli {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels et passé {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} prophètes au fil de l’épée. Je suis resté seul, et maintenant ils cherchent à m’ôter la vie. »
fr.R: Élie a répondu : « Je me suis donné de tout mon cœur pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées. Mais les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se sont détournés de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} alliance. Ils ont démoli {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels et tué {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} prophètes avec l’épée. Je suis le seul qui reste, et maintenant ils veulent me tuer moi aussi. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Nimekuwa na wivu mwingi kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, kwa maana wana wa Israeli wameliacha agano {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}; wamezibomoa madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}, na wamewaua manabii {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa upanga. Nami nimebaki, mimi peke yangu, nao wanautafuta uhai wangu, ili wauondoe."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Nimekuwa na wivu mwingi kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, kwa sababu Waisraeli wameliacha agano {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}. Wamezibomoa madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} na kuwaua manabii {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa upanga. Nimebaki mimi peke yangu, na sasa wanatafuta kuniua."
sw.R: Eliya akajibu, "Nimekutumikia kwa moyo wangu wote, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi. Lakini Waisraeli wameliacha agano {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}. Wamezibomoa madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} na kuwaua manabii {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa panga. Nimebaki mimi peke yangu, na sasa wanataka kuniua mimi pia."

vi.L: Ông thưa: "Con đã hết sức sốt sắng vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, vì con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đã lìa bỏ giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; họ đã phá đổ các bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và dùng gươm giết các nhà tiên tri của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Chỉ còn lại con, một mình con, và họ đang tìm mạng sống con để lấy đi."
vi.B: Ông thưa: "Con đã hết sức sốt sắng vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, vì dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã lìa bỏ giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. decisions.choice: being zealous I have been zealous: I have been jealous for the LORD's honor with all my strength
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the LORD's own jealousy for his people's loyalty (Exodus 20:5; 34:14), and of Phinehas, who acted against Israel's worship of the Baal of Peor (Numbers 25:11, 13). Repeating the verb makes it strong. Elijah means he has fought for the LORD alone against the worship of Baal.

decisions.choice: Yahweh God of hosts: the LORD who commands the armies of heaven and earth
decisions.reason: "Hosts" means armies. The title names the LORD as ruler over every power (1 Samuel 1:3; 17:45).

decisions.choice: I am left, I alone: Elijah's own view
decisions.reason: Elijah knows of the hundred prophets Obadiah hid (18:4, 13), so he may mean he is the only one still standing openly for the LORD. The LORD answers his words in verse 18.

decisions.choice: forsaken your covenant: the covenant made at Horeb
decisions.reason: Elijah speaks at the mountain where the covenant was given (verse 8; Deuteronomy 5:2). Tearing down the LORD's altars and killing his prophets (18:4, 30) are the signs that Israel has broken it.

decisions.choice: very zealous; worked with all my heart
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "zealous" so the link with Phinehas (Numbers 25:11) can be seen; the repeated verb becomes "very". Readable says what the zeal was.

decisions.choice: God of Armies
decisions.reason: As in the other books of Kings and Samuel, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts".

decisions.choice: "He sentido un vivo celo" (L); "un gran celo" (B); "He trabajado con todo mi corazón" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb of zeal for emphasis; Spanish "celo" keeps the jealousy for God's honor, and Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "plein de zèle, plein de zèle" (L); "rempli de zèle" (B); "je me suis donné de tout mon cœur" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the doubled verb; Literal and Balanced keep "zèle", the word that links Elijah with Phinehas, as the English.

decisions.choice: nimekuwa na wivu mwingi
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubled verb is jealousy for the LORD's honour; Swahili "wivu" keeps that sense, as God's own "wivu" in 14:22. Readable says he has served with all his heart, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Nimekutumikia ..., BWANA Mungu wa majeshi
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to God directly ("nimekutumikia"), so the name stands as an address; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân"
decisions.reason: The 2 Samuel wording for "the LORD God of hosts", the span on CHÚA only.

decisions.choice: "열심을 내고 또 열심을 냈습니다" (L), "온 힘을 다해 열심을 냈습니다" (B), "온 마음을 다해 일했습니다" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean "질투" would suggest envy; "열심" keeps the zeal for the LORD's honor that the meaning decision describes. Literal keeps the Hebrew doubling.

decisions.choice: tu (Elijah to the LORD): a tua aliança, os teus altares, os teus profetas
decisions.reason: Elijah speaks to the LORD with "tu" and the possessives that go with it, each under the deity_pronoun setting, as Romans 11:3 quotes this complaint in Portuguese ("os teus profetas ... os teus altares"). "Zeloso" (L, B) keeps the word of Phinehas' zeal in Numbers 25:11 in Portuguese (m1).

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B, R); no gender span
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas de Israel
decisions.reason: As in 18:20 and the Old Testament terms: "filhos de Israel" and "israelitas" already take in women and men, so Portuguese has no second wording for the English gender setting (also verse 14).

decisions.choice: look, Yahweh was passing by: the narrator tells what happened
alternatives: for look, Yahweh is about to pass by: still part of the LORD's words to Elijah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not mark where the LORD's words end. The participle "passing by" can describe what was happening or what was about to happen. Here the LORD's command is taken to end with "before Yahweh", and the rest is the narrator's account. Elijah does not actually go out until verse 13, so he seems to have stayed in the cave while the wind, earthquake and fire passed.

decisions.choice: Yahweh passing by: as the LORD passed by Moses on this mountain
decisions.reason: On the same mountain the LORD made his goodness "pass by" Moses, who was hidden in a cleft of the rock, and proclaimed his name (Exodus 33:19-22; 34:6). Elijah in his cave stands where Moses stood.

decisions.choice: wind and earthquake: signs of God's coming, but the LORD was not in them
decisions.reason: When the LORD came down on Sinai, the mountain shook and there was fire and storm (Exodus 19:16-18; compare Judges 5:4-5; Psalm 18:8-16). Here those signs come, but the narrator says each time that the LORD was not in them. He does not say that God has stopped using such powers: he sent fire on Carmel only days before (18:38).

decisions.choice: a wind: moving air, a storm wind
decisions.reason: The word can also mean "breath" or "spirit", but beside the earthquake and fire it is a storm that splits rocks.

decisions.choice: A mighty, fierce wind was splitting ... and smashing
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the strength of the wind and the force of its work in plain, vivid words.

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said"; the speaker is the LORD, whose word came to Elijah in verse 9.

decisions.choice: Akasema (no span)
decisions.reason: The English Literal "he" has a span; Swahili carries it in the verb prefix, which takes none.

source.text: וְאַחַ֤ר הָרַ֨עַשׁ֙ אֵ֔שׁ לֹ֥א בָאֵ֖שׁ יְהוָ֑ה וְאַחַ֣ר הָאֵ֔שׁ ק֖וֹל דְּמָמָ֥ה דַקָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And after the earthquake a fire; not in the fire [was] Yahweh; and after the fire a sound of silence thin.

en.L: And after the earthquake, a fire; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] not in the fire. And after the fire, a sound of thin silence.
en.B: Then came fire after the earthquake, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not in the fire. And when the fire had passed, a faint sound, thin as silence.
en.R: Next there was a fire. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not in the fire. When the fire was over, there was a very soft sound, almost like silence.

es.L: Y tras el terremoto, un fuego; {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no [estaba] en el fuego. Y tras el fuego, un sonido de silencio delgado.
es.B: Después del terremoto vino un fuego, pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no estaba en el fuego. Y cuando el fuego pasó, un sonido apenas perceptible, tenue como el silencio.
es.R: Después hubo un fuego. Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no estaba en el fuego. Cuando el fuego terminó, se oyó un sonido muy suave, casi como el silencio.

fr.L: Et après le tremblement de terre, un feu ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [n’était] pas dans le feu. Et après le feu, un son de fin silence.
fr.B: Après le tremblement de terre vint un feu, mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’était pas dans le feu. Et après le feu, un son ténu, fin comme le silence.
fr.R: Ensuite il y a eu un feu. Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’était pas dans le feu. Quand le feu a été passé, il y a eu un bruit très doux, presque comme un silence.

sw.L: Na baada ya tetemeko la nchi, moto; lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [hakuwa] katika moto. Na baada ya moto, sauti ya ukimya mwembamba.
sw.B: Baada ya tetemeko la nchi ukaja moto, lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuwa katika moto huo. Na moto ulipopita, sauti hafifu, nyembamba kama ukimya.
sw.R: Kisha kukawa na moto. Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuwa katika moto. Moto ulipokwisha, kukawa na sauti ndogo sana, karibu kama ukimya.

vi.L: Sau trận động đất, một ngọn lửa; [nhưng] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không ở trong ngọn lửa. Sau ngọn lửa, một âm thanh của sự im lặng mỏng manh.
vi.B: Sau trận động đất là lửa, nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không ở trong lửa. Sau khi lửa qua đi, có một tiếng động khẽ khàng, mỏng như sự im lặng.
vi.R: Kế đến có một ngọn lửa. Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không ở trong ngọn lửa. Khi lửa tắt, có một tiếng động thật khẽ, gần như im lặng.

ko.L: 그리고 지진 뒤에 불이 [있었으나], 불 속에도 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 [계시지] 않았다. 그리고 불 뒤에 가는 침묵의 소리가 [있었다].
ko.B: 지진이 지나간 뒤에 불이 일어났으나, 불 속에도 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 계시지 않았다. 불이 지나간 뒤에 침묵처럼 가느다란 소리가 있었다.
ko.R: 그다음에는 불이 일어났다. 그러나 불 속에도 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 계시지 않았다. 불이 꺼지자, 거의 침묵과 같은 아주 작은 소리가 들렸다.

pt.L: E depois do terremoto, um fogo; {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} não [estava] no fogo. E depois do fogo, um som de silêncio fino.
pt.B: Depois do terremoto veio um fogo, mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} não estava no fogo. E, quando o fogo passou, um som tênue, fino como o silêncio.
pt.R: Depois veio um fogo. Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} não estava no fogo. Quando o fogo acabou, houve um som muito suave, quase como o silêncio.

decisions.choice: a sound of thin silence: a sound so faint it is almost silence
alternatives: a still small voice (an older rendering)
decisions.reason: The first word means "sound" or "voice". The second means stillness or silence: the calm after a storm (Psalm 107:29), or the hush before a voice is heard (Job 4:16). The third means thin, fine, or crushed small, like the fine flakes of manna (Exodus 16:14) or finely ground incense (Leviticus 16:12). Put together they make a deliberate puzzle: a sound that is hardly a sound. Some take it as a gentle whisper or a soft breath of air. The text does not say that the LORD was in this sound, but after it the voice speaks (verse 13).

decisions.choice: fire: the LORD was not in it either
decisions.reason: Fire was the sign of the LORD's presence at Sinai (Exodus 19:18) and the answer to Elijah's prayer on Carmel (18:38). Here, after wind, earthquake and fire, the LORD comes to Elijah in near silence.

decisions.choice: a faint sound, thin as silence; a very soft sound, almost like silence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the paradox of the Hebrew, a sound that is close to silence, rather than settle it as a whisper or a breeze.

decisions.choice: a sound of thin silence, not "a still small voice"
decisions.reason: "A still small voice" is the King James Version's well-known wording. It keeps "small" for the third word but turns the silence into a voice, which the Hebrew does not say until verse 13. "A gentle whisper" makes it a sound of speech. Our wording keeps the stillness the Hebrew names.

decisions.choice: "un sonido de silencio delgado" (L); "un sonido apenas perceptible, tenue como el silencio" (B); "un sonido muy suave, casi como el silencio" (R)
decisions.reason: Each level follows the English reading of the three Hebrew words, a sound so faint it is almost silence, and avoids the traditional Spanish phrasing.

decisions.choice: "un son de fin silence" (L); "un son ténu, fin comme le silence" (B); "un bruit très doux, presque comme un silence" (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the paradox of the Hebrew, a sound that is almost silence, and avoids the familiar wording of other French Bibles.

decisions.choice: sauti ya ukimya mwembamba (Literal); sauti hafifu, nyembamba kama ukimya (Balanced); sauti ndogo sana, karibu kama ukimya (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the Hebrew's "silence" and "thin", as the English does, and avoids the familiar wording of older Swahili Bibles.

decisions.choice: "âm thanh của sự im lặng mỏng manh" (L); "tiếng động khẽ khàng, mỏng như sự im lặng" (B); "tiếng động thật khẽ, gần như im lặng" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of a thin silence, a sound almost beyond hearing; the familiar "still small voice" wording is avoided, as the English decision explains.

decisions.choice: "가는 침묵의 소리" (L), "침묵처럼 가느다란 소리" (B), "거의 침묵과 같은 아주 작은 소리" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads a sound so faint it is almost silence; the familiar "세미한 소리" of older Korean Bibles is not used, as the English sets aside "a still small voice".

decisions.choice: um som de silêncio fino (L); um som tênue, fino como o silêncio (B); um som muito suave, quase como o silêncio (R)
alternatives: o murmúrio de uma brisa leve
um cicio tranquilo e suave (older Portuguese rendering)
decisions.reason: Each level follows the English and m1: a sound so faint that it is almost silence, a deliberate paradox. "Um sussurro suave" would make it a sound of speech, and "o murmúrio de uma brisa leve" a breeze, readings m1 mentions but the Hebrew does not settle; the well-known older Portuguese wording turns the silence into a soft voice. "Som" keeps the word that becomes "uma voz" in verse 13 as close as Portuguese allows (m2 there).

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיָּ֤לֶט פָּנָיו֙ בְּאַדַּרְתּ֔וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֕א וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ ק֔וֹל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַה־לְּךָ֥ פֹ֖ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard Elijah, and he wrapped his face in his cloak, and went out and stood [at the] entrance of the cave; and look! to him a voice, and it said, What to you here, Elijah?

en.L: And it happened, when Elijah heard [it], that he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And look, a voice [came] to him and said, "What [is it] to you here, Elijah?"
en.B: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his cloak around his face, went out, and stood at the cave's mouth. Then a voice came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
en.R: When Elijah heard the sound, he covered his face with his cloak. He went out and stood at the opening of the cave. Then a voice said to him, "Elijah, what are you doing here?"

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Elías [lo] oyó, se cubrió el rostro con su manto y salió y se puso a la entrada de la cueva. Y he aquí que una voz [vino] a él y dijo: «¿Qué [haces] tú aquí, Elías?».
es.B: Cuando Elías lo oyó, se cubrió el rostro con su manto, salió y se puso a la entrada de la cueva. Entonces una voz vino a él: «¿Qué haces aquí, Elías?».
es.R: Cuando Elías oyó el sonido, se cubrió la cara con su manto. Salió y se quedó de pie a la entrada de la cueva. Entonces una voz le dijo: «Elías, ¿qué haces aquí?».

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Élie [l’]entendit, qu’il s’enveloppa le visage de son manteau, sortit et se tint à l’entrée de la grotte. Et voici, une voix [vint] à lui et dit : « Qu’as-tu [à faire] ici, Élie ? »
fr.B: Quand Élie l’entendit, il s’enveloppa le visage de son manteau, sortit et se tint à l’entrée de la grotte. Alors une voix lui parvint : « Que fais-tu ici, Élie ? »
fr.R: Quand Élie a entendu le bruit, il s’est couvert le visage avec son manteau. Il est sorti et s’est tenu à l’entrée de la grotte. Alors une voix lui a dit : « Élie, que fais-tu ici ? »

sw.L: Ikawa, Eliya aliposikia, akaufunika uso wake kwa joho lake, akatoka, akasimama mlangoni pa pango. Na tazama, sauti [ikamjia], ikasema, "Una nini hapa, Eliya?"
sw.B: Eliya alipoisikia, akajifunika uso kwa joho lake, akatoka, akasimama mdomoni mwa pango. Ndipo sauti ikamjia: "Unafanya nini hapa, Eliya?"
sw.R: Eliya alipoisikia sauti hiyo, akaufunika uso wake kwa joho lake. Akatoka nje, akasimama mlangoni pa pango. Ndipo sauti ikamwambia, "Eliya, unafanya nini hapa?"

vi.L: Xảy ra, khi Ê-li nghe [tiếng ấy], ông lấy áo choàng che mặt, đi ra đứng ở cửa hang. Kìa, có tiếng [đến] với ông, phán: "Ngươi làm gì ở đây, hỡi Ê-li?"
vi.B: Khi Ê-li nghe tiếng ấy, ông lấy áo choàng che mặt, đi ra đứng ở cửa hang. Bấy giờ có tiếng phán với ông: "Ê-li, con làm gì ở đây?"
vi.R: Khi Ê-li nghe tiếng ấy, ông lấy áo choàng che mặt. Ông đi ra đứng ở cửa hang. Rồi có tiếng phán với ông: "Ê-li, con đang làm gì ở đây?"

ko.L: 그리고 엘리야가 [그것을] 들었을 때, 그가 자기 겉옷으로 얼굴을 감싸고 나가서 굴 입구에 섰다. 그런데 보라, 한 소리가 그에게 [임하여] 말했다. "엘리야야, 여기서 너에게 무슨 [일이냐]?"
ko.B: 엘리야는 그 소리를 듣자 겉옷으로 얼굴을 감싸고 나가서 굴 어귀에 섰다. 그때 한 소리가 그에게 들려왔다. "엘리야야, 너는 여기서 무엇을 하고 있느냐?"
ko.R: 엘리야는 그 소리를 듣고 겉옷으로 얼굴을 가렸다. 그는 밖으로 나가 굴 입구에 섰다. 그때 한 소리가 그에게 말했다. "엘리야야, 너는 여기서 무엇을 하고 있느냐?"

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando Elias [o] ouviu, envolveu o rosto no seu manto, e saiu, e ficou de pé à entrada da caverna. E eis que uma voz [veio] a ele e disse: "Que [há] para ti aqui, Elias?"
pt.B: Quando Elias ouviu, cobriu o rosto com o manto, saiu e ficou de pé à entrada da caverna. Então uma voz veio a ele: "Que fazes aqui, Elias?"
pt.R: Quando Elias ouviu o som, cobriu o rosto com o seu manto. Ele saiu e ficou de pé na entrada da caverna. Então uma voz lhe disse: "Elias, o que estás fazendo aqui?"

decisions.choice: he wrapped his face in his cloak: in awe of God's presence
decisions.reason: Moses hid his face at the burning bush because he was afraid to look at God (Exodus 3:6), and on this mountain no one could see the LORD's face and live (Exodus 33:20-23). Elijah covers his face because he knows the LORD is near.

decisions.choice: a voice: the same word as "sound" in verse 12
decisions.reason: The faint "sound" of verse 12 now becomes a "voice" that speaks. The word is the same.

decisions.choice: cloak: a prophet's outer garment
decisions.reason: The word names a wide outer robe. Elijah's cloak will be thrown over Elisha (verse 19) and later parts the Jordan (2 Kings 2:8, 13-14).

decisions.choice: What are you doing here, Elijah?: the question of verse 9 repeated
decisions.reason: The LORD asks the same question in the same words, after all Elijah has seen and heard.

decisions.choice: cloak
decisions.reason: "Cloak" is used rather than the older word "mantle", here and in verse 19.

decisions.choice: "su manto"
decisions.reason: The prophet's outer garment, which passes to Elisha in verse 19; one Spanish word throughout.

decisions.choice: joho
decisions.reason: A prophet's outer cloak is "joho" at every level, the word that returns when Elijah throws it over Elisha (verse 19).

decisions.choice: "tiếng" for both "sound" (verse 12) and "voice"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "tiếng" covers both, as the Hebrew word does, so the link between the faint sound and the voice is kept.

decisions.choice: o manto (also verse 19)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Elijah's wide outer robe (m3), the sign of the prophet that passes to Elisha (verse 19; 2 Kings 2:13-14), is "o manto", the Portuguese word for a long outer garment; "capa" is kept for the different garment Ahijah tore (11:29). The LORD's question keeps the words of verse 9 at each level (m4).

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ קַנֹּ֨א קִנֵּ֜אתִי לַיהוָ֣ה׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֗וֹת כִּֽי־עָזְב֤וּ בְרִֽיתְךָ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתֶ֣יךָ הָרָ֔סוּ וְאֶת־נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ הָרְג֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב וָאִוָּתֵ֤ר אֲנִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י וַיְבַקְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Being zealous I have been zealous for Yahweh God of hosts, for have forsaken your covenant [the] sons of Israel; your altars they have torn down, and your prophets they have killed with the sword; and am left I, I alone, and they seek my life to take it.

en.L: And he said, "I have been very zealous for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts, for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant; they have torn down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, and they have killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets with the sword. And I am left, I alone, and they seek my life, to take it."
en.B: He answered, "I have been very zealous for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant. They have torn down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets to the sword. I alone am left, and now they are seeking to take my life."
en.R: Elijah answered, "I have worked with all my heart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies. But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant. They have torn down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars and killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets with swords. I am the only one left, and now they want to kill me too."

es.L: Y él dijo: «He sentido un vivo celo por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los ejércitos, porque los hijos de Israel han abandonado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pacto; han derribado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares y han matado a espada a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} profetas. Y he quedado yo, yo solo, y buscan mi vida para quitármela».
es.B: Él respondió: «He sentido un gran celo por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los Ejércitos, porque los israelitas han abandonado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pacto. Han derribado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares y han pasado a espada a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} profetas. Solo quedo yo, y ahora me buscan para quitarme la vida».
es.R: Elías respondió: «He trabajado con todo mi corazón para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de los Ejércitos. Pero los israelitas se han apartado de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pacto. Han derribado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares y han matado a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} profetas a espada. Soy el único que queda, y ahora quieren matarme a mí también».

fr.L: Et il dit : « J’ai été plein de zèle, plein de zèle pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées, car les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ont abandonné {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} alliance ; ils ont démoli {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels, et ils ont tué {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} prophètes par l’épée. Et je suis resté, moi seul, et ils cherchent ma vie pour me l’ôter. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « J’ai été rempli de zèle pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées, parce que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont abandonné {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} alliance. Ils ont démoli {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels et passé {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} prophètes au fil de l’épée. Je suis resté seul, et maintenant ils cherchent à m’ôter la vie. »
fr.R: Élie a répondu : « Je me suis donné de tout mon cœur pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées. Mais les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se sont détournés de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} alliance. Ils ont démoli {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels et tué {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} prophètes avec l’épée. Je suis le seul qui reste, et maintenant ils veulent me tuer moi aussi. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Nimekuwa na wivu mwingi kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, kwa maana wana wa Israeli wameliacha agano {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}; wamezibomoa madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}, na wamewaua manabii {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa upanga. Nami nimebaki, mimi peke yangu, nao wanautafuta uhai wangu, ili wauondoe."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Nimekuwa na wivu mwingi kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, kwa sababu Waisraeli wameliacha agano {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}. Wamezibomoa madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} na kuwaua manabii {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa upanga. Nimebaki mimi peke yangu, na sasa wanatafuta kuniua."
sw.R: Eliya akajibu, "Nimekutumikia kwa moyo wangu wote, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi. Lakini Waisraeli wameliacha agano {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}. Wamezibomoa madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} na kuwaua manabii {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa panga. Nimebaki mimi peke yangu, na sasa wanataka kuniua mimi pia."

vi.L: Ông thưa: "Con đã hết sức sốt sắng vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, vì con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đã lìa bỏ giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; họ đã phá đổ các bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và dùng gươm giết các nhà tiên tri của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Chỉ còn lại con, một mình con, và họ đang tìm mạng sống con để lấy đi."
vi.B: Ông thưa: "Con đã hết sức sốt sắng vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, vì dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã lìa bỏ giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. decisions.choice: Hazael and Aram: the kingdom of the Arameans, whose capital was Damascus
decisions.reason: Aram lay north-east of Israel, with Damascus as its capital, and was often at war with Israel (20:1; 22:1-4). Hazael was an official of its king Ben-hadad (2 Kings 8:7-15).

decisions.choice: anoint: pour oil on someone to set them apart for an office
decisions.reason: Kings were anointed (1 Samuel 10:1; 16:13), and so were priests (Exodus 29:7). Only here is a prophet told to anoint another prophet (verse 16).

decisions.choice: the three anointings: how they were carried out
decisions.reason: Elijah himself does not anoint Hazael or Jehu. He calls Elisha by throwing his cloak over him (verse 19). Later Elisha tells Hazael that he will be king (2 Kings 8:13), and a young prophet sent by Elisha anoints Jehu (2 Kings 9:1-6). The LORD's commission is fulfilled through Elijah's successor.

decisions.choice: go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus: go back north, toward Damascus
decisions.reason: Elijah is to go back the way he came, and on past Israel to the wilderness near Damascus. The man who ran from Jezebel is sent back into danger with a task.

decisions.choice: Jehu son of Nimshi: a commander who would end Ahab's dynasty
decisions.reason: Jehu was a commander in Israel's army. He became king by overthrowing Ahab's son Joram and destroying Ahab's family and the worship of Baal (2 Kings 9-10). He is called "son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi" in 2 Kings 9:2, so "son" here means descendant.

decisions.choice: Abel-meholah: a town in the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: The town lay near the Jordan, south of the Sea of Galilee (Judges 7:22; 1 Kings 4:12).

decisions.choice: as prophet in your place: as your successor
decisions.reason: Elijah has said he is the only one left (verses 10, 14). The LORD names another to carry on his work after him.

decisions.choice: from the town of Abel-meholah
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so the reader knows this is a place name.
